implement: skill://legion-worker: the phase contract this implementer runs under — the shared workspace, the push and handoff rules, the pull-request body and its proofs.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the definition of a proof (command, surface, observed, head SHA, negative control) that every entry of the implement handoff's proof array must meet, and the simplify pass on the settled head.

skill://ce-simplify-code: the change edits two dozen manifests, workflows and guides mechanically and adds two new shell scripts; the simplify pass is where the repetition and the second convention get caught.
skill://dispatch: required before any write to Dispatch, which the implementer makes when it reports on the issue.
test: skill://legion-worker: the tester drives the changed surface and does not re-run CI's static lanes.
skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: what the tester verifies in the implementer's proof and what its own E2E line and proof array must carry.

plan.md section 4 and task T13: each acceptance criterion's surface and command are written to be re-run as given, and T13 gives the recipe for the container state AC1 needs (a copy with no node_modules, poisoned by one `bunx biome check .`).
review: skill://legion-worker: the review round's order and the reviewer's own handoff fields.
skill://legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: one disposition reply per thread, resolved one by one, never in bulk.
skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the approval of the head, retro, READY and what READY refuses.
plan.md section 8: the five departures from the approved spec that the reviewer reads beside the spec.

findings.finding: F1: the setup argv runs where the script does not exist (the controller's /legion, theorem-labs/agent-infra, any branch older than the merge), and a missing file is a non-zero exit that holds the issue, not the no-op the spec claims.
findings.answer: Design decision D8 and section 8 departure 4: the plan gives the deployment's line verbatim, `[/bin/sh, -c, 'if [ -r ./scripts/legion-setup.sh ]; then sh ./scripts/legion-setup.sh; fi']`, as the payload of the architect's child issue, and records the correction to the spec's sentence. Task T8 step 2 also exits 0 silently when the working directory has no bun.lock.

findings.finding: F2: AC4's first-turn notice needs a pi-legion change, which only a new worker image delivers; a setup command cannot set the environment variable the existing notice rides on.
findings.answer: Design decision D7 and task T10: the script writes a file, pi-legion reads it at session_start and reuses the notice mechanism. Section 5 states that the image must be built from this merge commit and that the child issue must say so; section 8 departure 1 records the reading of the spec's wording.

findings.finding: F3: a cache on the issue disk reverses the policy manifest_test.go:658-671 pins (one shared bun cache hardlinked into many worktrees, LEGION-198), and the spec does not say where on the disk.
findings.answer: Design decision D4: the cache goes on the issue volume outside the workspace (/legion/bun/cache, derived as ${LEGION_WORKSPACE%/workspaces/*}), because an issue's volume holds exactly one workspace, so the hardlinks reach that one node_modules and no other checkout. Set by the script, not the manifest, so no daemon change and no daemon release. Task T12 adds the sentence to that test's comment so the repository does not carry two contradictory statements.

findings.finding: F4: 'once per issue' is the wrong key — a forward merge moves bun.lock mid-issue, leaving node_modules that no longer match the lock.
findings.answer: Design decision D5 and task T8 step 4: the marker holds `cksum < bun.lock` and is honoured only while node_modules/.bin/biome is also present. Task T9 covers both ('marker matches but node_modules removed' reinstalls). Section 8 departure 2 records it.

findings.finding: F5: bun install peaks near 0.8 GiB while the architect, planner, reviewer and merger containers default to a 1 Gi memory limit.
findings.answer: Design decision D9: an OOM-killed install is an ordinary failure — report, exit 0, no marker, the next role installs. Task T9 tests a SIGKILLed child (137). Section 7 item 2 puts the alternative (a memory bump as a second deployment line) to the architect.

findings.finding: F6: the install's wall time is unmeasured, and it competes with the 360 s registration deadline on every start; nothing says what a role does when it cannot take the lock.
findings.answer: Section 1 cites the architect's measurement in the spec (1,986 packages, 54 s, 1.4 GiB; 0.3 s on a second install). Task T8 step 9 sets a 90 s lock wait and a 180 s install timeout, both overridable through the environment, worst case 270 s inside 360 s. A lock it cannot take is a reported failure and exit 0, never a wait — the human's rider says a failure must not block the work.

findings.finding: F7: the frozen install is not npm-only — bun.lock:233,2096 carry a github: dependency (proof-sdk-upstream), whose egress and credential are unproven.
findings.answer: Section 1 records that the architect's measured install of all 1,986 packages succeeded in a container of this pod, which covers that dependency. Task T13 and section 4's AC3 row re-run the real install in the throwaway copy, so the implementer confirms it rather than assuming it; a failure there is a finding for the architect, not a plan detail.

findings.finding: F8: a report at a fixed path under LEGION_STATE_DIR is read by more sessions than the one it was written for — the directory outlives a generation in a pod, and under tmux is shared by every pane of the host.
findings.answer: Design decision D7 and task T8 step 8: the record carries issue, role and generation; task T10's reader returns nothing unless all three match its own environment, and a successful install deletes the record. Task T9 and T10's tests cover both directions.

findings.finding: F9: a guard that forbids `bunx` outright trips on worker.Dockerfile:492, on check-release-credentials.sh:164, and on the two notes that record this defect.
findings.answer: Task T6: the rule is 'a prescribed command invokes a pinned check tool through scripts/repo-tool.sh', judged on parsed package.json script values, parsed workflow run values, shell files and fenced code blocks — prose and inline code are never judged, .github/scripts/ is excluded as the guards' own text, and a marked block is exempt with its reason. Its .test.sh pins exactly those lines as negative cases that pass.

findings.finding: F10: `bunx playwright` is a test command AC2's body covers and its enumeration omits.
findings.answer: Design decision D3: in scope. Tasks T2 and T3 convert the three dispatch e2e recipes, docs.yaml:87, envoy-and-contracts.yaml:701,732 and the two media scripts; T6's tool list names playwright. Section 8 departure 5 records the widening.

findings.finding: F11: the root manifest has no lint, typecheck or test recipe, and two CI steps check scripts/dispatch and scripts/github-apps, which no package recipe reaches.
findings.answer: Task T2 adds root `lint` and `typecheck` recipes through the wrapper, which passes paths and `-p <tsconfig>` through; task T3 rewrites all five CI steps, and says that leaving pr-and-main.yaml:111 would make the required lint job fail its own new guard.

findings.finding: F12: docs/site's bare `biome` and `tsc` recipes are the silently-wrong-tool case, since the worker image puts tsc 5.9.3 on PATH.
findings.answer: Measurement M5 and design decision D1: the wrapper resolves node_modules/.bin explicitly and never PATH. Task T2 routes docs/site's two recipes through it, and task T6 rule 1 judges a bare pinned check tool in a recipe, not only `bunx`.

findings.finding: F13: three of the guides AC2 names already prescribe `bun run` and need no edit.
findings.answer: Task T4's last bullet names packages/proof-editor/AGENTS.md:166-171, packages/dispatch/README.md:33-36 and docs/site/README.md:19 as correct unchanged, satisfied transitively once T2 pins their recipes.

findings.finding: F14: AGENTS.md:52 asserts a reason that is false in a role container; a reader who keeps the sentence will put the command back.
findings.answer: Task T4's first bullet deletes the claim as well as the command, and replaces it with what a role container actually does. Task T5 rewrites the rule sections of the two docs/solutions notes that teach the same thing.

findings.finding: F15: 'nothing on the container's own disk' is a hard ephemeral-storage limit, and it also forbids the obvious way to test the script (a scratch install under /tmp).
findings.answer: Design decision D4 and task T8 step 10 keep every write under the issue volume and LEGION_STATE_DIR; task T13 step 2 puts the throwaway copy on the issue volume (/legion/infra-71-proof, measurement M6) and never under /tmp or $HOME; section 4's AC3 row makes the absence a measured check (find listings before and after), not an assumption.

findings.finding: F16: running the install in this issue's own shared workspace destroys the state AC1 must be reproduced in and reaches every later role of the issue.
findings.answer: Task T13: AC1 and AC2 are proven first, while the workspace has no node_modules; every install proof, and the new unit tests, run in the throwaway copy, which is removed before the phase completes; the implement handoff records whether the shared workspace holds node_modules and gives the tester the recipe for AC1's state.

findings.finding: F17: AC1 has no machine check as written — it quantifies over prose.
findings.answer: Section 4 splits it: the guard of T6 (and its test) is the standing machine check that no prescriptive file carries the vulnerable form, and the AC1 row is a re-runnable manual proof in the poisoned container, with the pre-change behaviour as its negative control.

findings.finding: F18: AC5's 'its own download cache does not grow' contradicts a cache shared by the issue.
findings.answer: Section 4's AC5 row restates it against the shared cache (its size unchanged, no file under node_modules newer, bun never run), with the note that a second role has no cache of its own once the cache is per issue. Section 7 item 3 and section 8 departure 3 put the wording to the architect.

findings.finding: F19: the pi-legion change's release surface — version, changelog, and whether the plugin interface or daemon contract moves.
findings.answer: Task T10's last bullet: one entry in packages/pi-legion/CHANGELOG.md's existing [Unreleased] Added section, no daemon API contract bump and no plugin interface bump, with the reason stated in the entry (the notice crosses no daemon RPC and no @legion/pi-shared interface). The version is CI's to write, not the implementer's.

findings.finding: F20: portability — flock and timeout are Linux, and the wrapper is run by humans on their own machines; the install script needs a test runnable on the CI runner.
findings.answer: Design decision D6: the install script exits 0 silently with LEGION_WORKSPACE unset, so its Linux-only tools never reach a developer's machine; task T1 keeps the wrapper POSIX sh with no such dependency. Task T9 adds scripts/legion-setup.test.sh, run against a stubbed bun with no network and wired into the test job beside the other .test.sh steps.

specDepartures.spec: The failure is recorded where the role's agent reads it in its first turn, 'by the path Legion already uses to tell an agent that its workspace was recreated'.
specDepartures.plan: The script writes a JSON record to $LEGION_STATE_DIR/legion-setup-report.json and a new pi-legion module reads it at session_start, reusing the existing notice mechanism rather than its transport.
specDepartures.evidence: That path is an environment variable the launcher sets (packages/daemon/internal/launcher/launcher.go:271), and the setup command runs in a subshell before `exec "$@"` (packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins.go:134-147), so it can set nothing for the agent's process.

specDepartures.spec: The install 'happens once for an issue rather than once for each of its six roles', with a guard in the workspace that records success only.
specDepartures.plan: The guard's marker holds a digest of bun.lock and is honoured only while node_modules/.bin/biome is present, so a lockfile that moves mid-issue installs again.
specDepartures.evidence: docs/solutions/legion/a-forward-merge-after-retro-reinstalls-when-main-bumped-the-lockfile-...-LEGION-634.md:67-71 records a forward merge moving bun.lock mid-issue and `tsc` failing until `bun install --frozen-lockfile` ran again.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance: 'A second role of the same issue, starting while the packages are already there, installs nothing: its own download cache does not grow and the packages are untouched.'
specDepartures.plan: Proven against the issue's one shared cache: its size is unchanged, no file under node_modules is newer, and bun is never run.
specDepartures.evidence: The same spec requires the cache on the issue's disk, which every role container of the pod mounts (docs/kubernetes.md:2125-2127), so no role has a download cache of its own to measure.

acceptance: A second role of the same issue, starting while the packages are already there, installs nothing: the issue's shared download cache does not grow, no file under node_modules is newer, and the install command is never run.

specDepartures.spec: 'The same command also runs where there is nothing to install: the project controller's container has no workspace at all, and the project's other repository carries no lock file. There the script does nothing, says nothing, and exits 0.'
specDepartures.plan: The deployment's one line tests for the script before running it: `[/bin/sh, -c, 'if [ -r ./scripts/legion-setup.sh ]; then sh ./scripts/legion-setup.sh; fi']`. The script itself still exits 0 silently with no bun.lock.
specDepartures.evidence: runtime.kubernetes.setup is one argv for the whole deployment (packages/daemon/internal/config/kubernetes.go:78-82); the controller's working directory is /legion with no checkout, and an issue on theorem-labs/agent-infra has no such file, so the shell's own 'not found' would be a non-zero exit, which stops that role's agent and ends in a held issue (plugins.go:144-150, docs/kubernetes.md:1282-1287).

summary: Where the script is not in the working directory at all — the controller's container, the project's other repository, a branch older than this change — the deployment's line runs nothing and exits 0; the script's own silence covers a checkout that has the script but no lock file.

specDepartures.spec: The other half of the fix is enumerated as the commands block in AGENTS.md, the same commands in README.md, the per-package guides, the ten lint recipes in the workspace manifests, and the notes under docs/solutions/.
specDepartures.plan: It also changes the ten typecheck recipes, the Playwright call sites (three recipes, three workflow steps, two media scripts), five CI steps, and the docs/solutions notes beyond the two that record this defect; docs/plans/ and docs/superpowers/ are left as the human-authored history they are.
specDepartures.evidence: The spec's own acceptance covers 'a command for lint, types or tests'; a bare `tsc` is answered by the worker image's own TypeScript at /usr/local/bin/tsc 5.9.3 (measured 2026-10-21 in this role container), and `bunx playwright` fetches whatever the registry serves rather than the @playwright/test bun.lock pins.

outcome.scope: Half A covers every prescribed lint, type and test command in the repository — the ten typecheck recipes, the Playwright call sites and the five CI steps included — not only the ten lint recipes and the files the spec enumerates.
